The contact-form call went through and returned a success message: *"Thank you for contacting us! We've received your message and will get back to you soon."*

However, the same confirmation-gate defect from the previous step reproduced here. The result carried `"_hint": "This tool required user confirmation (callbackMode=approve). The user confirmed execution, so the result is now available."` — yet no confirmation was ever surfaced to me or requested at any point. I sent the call with `callbackMode` left at the default (`wait`), and it executed and submitted immediately. The cortex tree now also shows `/memories/t7-approve-test` containing `T7_APPROVE_OK`, confirming the earlier `approve`-mode write likewise executed without a gate.

So the approval mechanism is auto-confirming instead of blocking: any tool that requires user confirmation runs straight through, and the `_hint` retroactively asserts a confirmation that never happened. That's a safety-relevant issue on a tool that sends real messages.

FAILED: confirmation gate does not block — contact-form submitted immediately and returned a _hint claiming the user confirmed execution, though no confirmation was ever requested (same auto-confirm defect as the T7a cortex-write approve call, which also executed and wrote /memories/t7-approve-test).
